answer: Sybil attacks fail when identity must be earned over a long horizon instead of minted cheaply. Require each agent to lock a slashable bond and emit a steady liveness pulse of verifiable, timestamped work; honest peers maintain a shared atlas mapping those heartbeats to accrued reputation. A thousand clones spun up overnight have no history on that atlas and no accumulated pulse, so their attestations carry near-zero weight until each pays real, time-bound cost — making forged majorities far more expensive than one genuine participant.
